exercise1.prompt: A Shape parent with draw(), and a Circle subclass that overrides it

cases.name: Circle is built from Shape and defines its own draw
cases.describe: a Circle class written as class Circle(Shape) with draw inside it

hiddenCases.name: Shape is the class that defines draw first
hiddenCases.describe: a Shape class with a draw of its own

hiddenCases.name: the parent's draw is left as it was
a Circle is still a Shape

exercise1.hint: The overriding method has to live inside Circle. A function of the same name written at the left margin is a different thing entirely, and Circle().draw() will still find the parent's.

exercise2.prompt: A Payment parent with two subclasses, each processed through the same loop

cases.name: both payment types are built from Payment and override process
cases.describe: CreditCard(Payment) and PayPal(Payment), each with its own process

hiddenCases.name: Payment is the class the two share
hiddenCases.describe: a Payment class with a process of its own

hiddenCases.name: a PayPal payment reports itself differently
the same call gives a different answer per object
the payments are walked with a loop, not written out one by one
hiddenCases.describe: a loop over the list of payments

exercise2.hint: The loop body does not know which kind of payment it is holding, and that is the point. Each subclass has to carry its own process for the same line to do different work.

questions.prompt: What is polymorphism, in one sentence?
choices: The same call doing the right thing for whichever object it lands on
A class that can change its own methods at runtime
Two functions with the same name in one file
questions.explain: The caller writes payment.process() once. Which version runs is decided by the object, not by the calling code.

questions.prompt: A subclass defines a method with the same name as its parent's. What happens?
choices: Python raises an error about the duplicate
The subclass's version is used for subclass objects, and the parent's is untouched
questions.explain: Lookup starts at the object's own class and stops at the first match. The parent's method is still there for the parent's own objects.

questions.prompt: Match each object to what payment.process() returns for it.
questions.explain: Each object finds the process defined nearest to it, which is its own class's if it has one.

questions.prompt: Writing the overriding method at the left margin instead of inside the class makes it an ordinary ___, and the object will still find the parent's method.
questions.explain: A method is a function that lives in a class body. Indentation is the whole difference, and it changes what the object can find.
